testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When entering traffic, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Be ready for your vehicle to accelerate slowly, especially if it is loaded.
Make sure you can cross traffic completely without interfering with other vehicles.
Assume other drivers will make room for your larger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your larger vehicle.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic, think about your vehicle's size and how much space it needs to accelerate. Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle before you start moving. Your vehicle needs more room if it is heavily loaded. Before crossing, make sure you can get all the way across without getting in the way of other traffic.

questions.question: If your brakes pull to one side when you use them, what does this mean?

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, there may be a brake problem. You should fix any brake issues before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle breaks federal and state laws.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, what should you check?

options.text: The lift is the proper color.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a cargo lift, check for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully folded down and locked securely.

questions.question: What might you be asked to do during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What could a cardboard box on the roadway mean?

options.text: It is not a cause for concern.
It may contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
You should drive off the roadway to avoid it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. Something that looks harmless, like a cardboard box, could hide a hard or heavy object that could seriously damage your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if a vehicle runs without engine oil?

options.text: The vehicle will get the best possible gas mileage.
The engine can be destroyed quickly.
The windshield wipers will not operate.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: The engine must have adequate oil pressure. An engine can be destroyed very quickly if it runs without oil.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Be especially careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal if the spring brakes are on. Using the brake pedal at the same time as spring brakes can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What must you provide to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: A list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.
Your work history for the last five years.

questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must give your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check.

questions.question: What can very hot temperatures cause?
questions.explanation: Air expands when it is hot, so tire pressure increases in hot weather. This can cause tire failure. Always check your tire pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: When approaching your vehicle, what should you check?

options.text: The vehicle is shinier than other vehicles.
The vehicle is not parked too close to other vehicles.
There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting your vehicle, check its overall condition and look for damage or tilting. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or tree limbs.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds how many feet to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, what happens?

options.text: ABS will still help you steer better.
ABS will make the trailer more likely to jackknife.
ABS will make your brake lights brighter.

questions.correctAnswerText: ABS will still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, ABS will still improve your steering control. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, where should you park?

options.text: In a crowded area near trees

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop right away. Park in an open area away from things that could catch fire, such as trees or other vehicles. Do not go to a service station.

questions.question: Where are ABS warning lamps on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have yellow warning lamps on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lamps on the left side, on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: Why is it most important to inspect your vehicle before a trip?
questions.explanation: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep yourself and others safe on the road. Pre-trip safety inspections are required by state and federal laws.

questions.question: Why do you need to drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs replacing
Because compressed air contains water that must be drained
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be drained
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What is the stab braking method for emergency stops?

options.text: Push the brakes fully until wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat
Apply brakes halfway while keeping wheels rolling
Push brakes fully, lock the wheels, and hold until the vehicle stops

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes fully until wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat
questions.explanation: Stab braking means pushing the brakes fully until they lock. Then release until the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process to stop.

questions.question: How is water and oil removed from air storage tanks?

options.text: Water and oil are siphoned out
A drain valve is opened to release the water and oil
Water and oil are removed automatically when brakes are used
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil

questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve is opened to release the water and oil
questions.explanation: A drain valve at the bottom of air storage tanks removes water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes. Manually operated tanks must be drained every day.

questions.question: How far behind your vehicle should warning devices be placed when stopped on a highway?
questions.explanation: When you stop on a highway, place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens when an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) fails?

options.text: A yellow lamp lights up on the instrument panel

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow lamp lights up on the instrument panel
questions.explanation: When ABS malfunctions, a yellow warning lamp on the instrument panel will light up to alert you.

questions.question: If you are convicted of an alcohol-related offense in your personal vehicle, what happens to your CDL?

options.text: Your CDL is only affected if you refused a breath test.
You lose your CDL for one year.
A sticker is placed on your CDL.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose your CDL for one year.
questions.explanation: If your driving privileges are revoked, canceled, or suspended for an alcohol-related offense, controlled substance offense, or felony, you will lose your CDL for one year.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after driving a short distance?

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the correct tire was changed.
Check for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop a short distance later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: How often should you stop for a break while driving to avoid fatigue?
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, stop for a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which of the following is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts
questions.explanation: Look for these exhaust problems: loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, or tailpipes; loose, broken, or missing brackets and clamps; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts or tires; and leaking exhaust parts. Exhaust parts that are NOT rubbing against fuel system parts is normal and not a problem.

questions.question: What type of licenses do most CDL holders have?
questions.explanation: Most CDL holders who drive commercial vehicles across state lines are non-excepted interstate commerce drivers.

questions.question: What does tire load mean?

options.text: The maximum air pressure a tire can hold
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure
The minimum safe weight a tire must carry
The average weight of all tires on a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control the vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: What can happen if you don't drain the air brake system tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
The brakes become soft and spongy.
Too much air collects in the system.
Too much fuel is carried in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil. If water builds up and freezes in cold weather, it can cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it.
Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Try to get another vehicle to push you.
Stay in the vehicle and wait for police.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, get out immediately and move away from the tracks. Find the emergency contact number on signs at the crossing and call it, or call 911.

questions.question: How can you tell if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: You must place emergency warning devices within ____ of stopping on the road shoulder.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road shoulder, place your emergency warning devices within 10 minutes. Also turn on your four-way emergency flashers.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
May face the road before completely exiting.
Must face away from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If your vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is using high beam headlights, you should:

options.text: Flash your high beams to tell the driver to use low beams.
Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull to the side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle approaches with high beam headlights, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until it passes. This prevents the bright lights from blinding you.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: Which action is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the back of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave open space on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side.
questions.explanation: When turning right, do not turn too wide to the left. Keep the back of your vehicle close to the curb. Leaving space on your right side may signal to other drivers that you are turning left, so they may try to pass you on the right.

questions.question: Which sign shows you are drowsy while driving?

options.text: Your eyes go out of focus on their own
You have trouble holding your head up

questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include your eyes closing or going out of focus by themselves, trouble keeping your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: In exercises other than straight line backing, you may exit your vehicle to check its position no more than:
questions.explanation: You may exit your vehicle to check its position during basic control skills test exercises. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you may look only once. For other exercises, you may look no more than twice.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Not make gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan trips with realistic times and allow extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane. Do not make gestures at other drivers, even minor ones like shaking your head.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on roads.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it may just look wet. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check tire inflation?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire inflation during the vehicle inspection test. Simply kicking the tires will not give you a passing score.

questions.question: What can change the height of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Heavy weight makes a vehicle sit lower than normal. An empty vehicle is taller than one carrying a heavy load. A vehicle that fits under a bridge when full may not fit when empty.

questions.question: Heavy steering is often a sign of:
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means one of your front tires has failed. If your steering feels different, pull off the road safely and check your tires.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Stay quiet and see if the problem goes away.
Write a report describing your concerns.
Try to fix the issue yourself.
Not use that part and hope others don't notice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing your concerns.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day, you may need to write a report on the vehicle. Write down any problems that could affect safety or cause mechanical failure.

questions.question: Where should a helper stand when backing a vehicle?

options.text: In front of the passenger side
In front of the driver side
On the side of the truck
Near the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck
questions.explanation: A helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them. Agree on hand signals before backing, including a signal for "stop."

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will:

options.text: Allow you to drive faster than normal.
Allow you to follow other vehicles more closely.
Allow you to drive less carefully.

questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control during hard braking. It does not always make you stop shorter.

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum happens when brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: More worn on the passenger's side.

questions.explanation: Check that the landing gear has no missing parts and is fully raised. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should not be damaged.

questions.question: What can happen if you use a parking brake in wet weather below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Using a parking brake in very wet, freezing weather can cause the brakes to freeze. This will prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are on the wheels and axles. The braking parts that stop the vehicle are inside the drum.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs approximately ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.
